evals.prompt: I want to add a multi-tenant workspace system to my existing single-tenant Laravel 13 + Inertia.js + React SaaS. Users should be able to create workspaces, invite team members, set roles (owner/admin/member/viewer), and switch between workspaces. Data isolation is critical — users must never see another workspace's data.
evals.expected_output: Route 3 (specific feature) plan, possibly escalating toward Route 1 scope. Should ask clarifying questions about data isolation strategy (row-level tenant_id scoping via global Eloquent scopes vs schema-per-tenant), existing Laravel auth setup (Sanctum/Fortify/Breeze), and billing implications per workspace. Plan document (PLAN_[timestamp]_${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}.md) includes: architecture decision on tenancy approach (clears the ADR 3-of-3 gate — hard to reverse, real trade-off — so emits an ADR and persists a durable copy per references/plan-templates.md), database migrations with tenant_id columns and foreign keys, global scope middleware for workspace scoping, Spatie Permission or custom role/permission system design, invitation flow with Laravel notifications, workspace switcher React component via Inertia, data isolation verification Pest tests. Runs the SaaS Concerns Checklist — Tenant isolation and RBAC/permissions dimensions are Required and feed into ## Files (scopes, policy classes) and ## Tests Required (cross-tenant invisibility + authorization tests). Plan items ordered by dependency (migration before middleware before UI). Each item has clear acceptance criteria. If 4+ tasks at Standard depth, generates .v-prompt-packs/v-plan-<MM-DD>/ with one self-contained /v prompt file per session for parallel execution.

evals.prompt: I just acquired a Laravel 13 SaaS codebase — 200+ Eloquent models, 100+ controllers, Blade frontend (no Inertia), zero documentation, minimal Pest tests, unclear service layer patterns. I need to understand how the codebase is organized before I start migrating to Inertia.js + React.
evals.expected_output: Route 2 (codebase understanding) plan. Exploration-heavy plan that maps: Eloquent model relationships and domain boundaries, controller organization and route grouping, service/action class patterns, job and queue inventory, API surface area from routes/api.php, database schema visualization from migrations, external service integrations (Stripe, S3, mail, etc.), Blade component and layout hierarchy. Plan should NOT propose code changes — it produces understanding artifacts: architecture diagram, Eloquent relationship map, route inventory, and a 'how things work' document with P0/P1/P2 gap analysis. Each exploration step has specific artisan/grep commands to run. Route 2 does NOT generate parallel prompt packs (no implementation). Should recommend v-check after understanding is established to find issues, and note that the Inertia migration itself would be a separate /v-plan Route 4 (refactor).

evals.prompt: My Laravel 13 + Inertia.js + React app has grown to 80+ Inertia pages and the Vite build is now painfully slow at 45 seconds. The JS bundle is 1.8MB. Inertia page loads feel sluggish — full page reloads instead of SPA navigation on some routes. We need a refactoring plan to improve performance — code splitting, lazy loading Inertia pages, removing unused npm packages, and optimizing the Vite config. Don't break anything.
evals.expected_output: Route 4 (refactor) plan. Should analyze current Vite bundle composition before proposing changes. Plan includes: Vite bundle analysis step (rollup-plugin-visualizer), npm dependency audit for unused/duplicate packages, Inertia lazy loading strategy with resolvePageComponent dynamic imports, React.lazy for heavy components, Vite chunk splitting configuration, image optimization pipeline, SSR evaluation if not already enabled. Each refactor item has: measurable before/after target (e.g., 'reduce bundle from 1.8MB to <800KB', 'Vite build from 45s to <15s'), rollback strategy in ## Rollback Notes, Pest + Vitest verification step. Plan orders items by risk (low-risk dependency removal first, high-risk Inertia lazy loading last). Includes a 'do not touch' list for stability-critical routes. May delegate prompt generation to /v-audit-code. Generates .v-prompt-packs/v-plan-<MM-DD>/ if 4+ items.

evals.prompt: My Laravel + Inertia SaaS has a signup-to-activation drop-off — only 18% of new signups reach their first 'aha' moment (creating their first project). I want a growth plan to lift activation: onboarding checklist, empty-state guidance, and a couple of A/B tests. I have Plausible analytics but no funnel events instrumented yet.
evals.expected_output: Route 5 (growth planning) plan. Should ask which funnel stage to focus on (Activation), whether baseline metrics exist (partial — Plausible but no funnel events), and the growth target. Plan document includes FUNNEL_BASELINE (current 18% activation with confidence caveat since events aren't instrumented yet), GROWTH_TARGET (quantified), BOTTLENECK_ANALYSIS (activation stage), GROWTH_EXPERIMENTS prioritized by impact/effort (onboarding checklist, empty-state guidance, activation-nudge email), A_B_TEST_PLAN with control/treatment/sample-size/duration/statistical-test, IMPLEMENTATION_ORDER by impact/effort ratio, MONITORING_DASHBOARD, and ROLLBACK_CRITERIA for stopping an experiment. First step must be instrumenting activation funnel events (the plan can't optimize what it can't measure). SaaS Concerns Checklist applies (analytics instrumentation Required). Per the zero-outreach operator constraint, all growth levers are passive/product-side (in-app onboarding, empty states, lifecycle email) — no outbound/paid/PR motions. Generates .v-prompt-packs/v-plan-<MM-DD>/ (Measurement → Experiment → Optimization sessions) if 4+ tasks.

evals.prompt: I need to plan a change to my ~/.claude Stop hook so that planning-only sessions that also touched a single docs file still pass the completion gate. The hook is check-review-artifact.sh and there's a PLANNING_PASS marker path involved.
evals.expected_output: Route 6 (User-Owned Maintenance) — triggered by 'hook'/'.claude'/'maintenance' keywords. Because the target paths are already named and this is owner-managed infra, the DEFAULT is a lightweight inline checklist routed straight to /v-maintenance, NOT a full multi-section PLAN artifact (per SKILL.md Route 6 note + references/route-guides.md Route 6). Since this is a hook/gate change under hooks/, the plan must call out: path scoping (canonical ~/.claude, honoring canonical-vs-mirror policy), targeted tests only (the specific check-review-artifact test, never the full suite during iteration), a required content-validated BITE_LEDGER (red≠0/green=0) proving each guard bites via swap-audit, and a hostile-review focus (false-green gate / marker-forgery / self-modification-denial). Should NOT pad this into a heavyweight PLAN unless the user explicitly asks for a written plan or the change spans many files with real rollback risk.

evals.prompt: [V_DEPTH=1] --detail=standard Refactor and clean up our onboarding flow to improve the signup conversion funnel and lift activation.
evals.expected_output: Headless auto-routing test (V_DEPTH=1, so entry-point questions are skipped and Standard depth is used). The prompt matches BOTH Route 4 (refactor/clean up/improve) and Route 5 (conversion funnel/activation) keyword sets. Per the mandatory first-match precedence rule (specific-domain signals outrank generic change-verbs; growth keywords are checked before refactor keywords), this MUST route deterministically to Route 5 (Growth Planning), not Route 4 — the growth/funnel/activation intent is more specific than the generic 'refactor/clean up/improve' verbs. The same prompt must route the same way on repeat headless invocations (no run-to-run drift). Produces a Route 5 growth plan (FUNNEL_BASELINE, BOTTLENECK_ANALYSIS on activation, GROWTH_EXPERIMENTS, A_B_TEST_PLAN) at Standard depth with effort estimates and, if 4+ tasks, a .v-prompt-packs/v-plan-<MM-DD>/ pack. No AskUserQuestion prompts are issued (V_DEPTH>=1).
